```python your_code_here
class Settings:
    DATABASE_URL: str = os.getenv("DATABASE_URL", "sqlite:///./photos.db")
    MEDIA_ROOT: str = os.getenv("MEDIA_ROOT", "./media")
    ADMIN_TOKEN: str = os.getenv("ADMIN_TOKEN", "changeme")
    MAX_IMAGE_BYTES: int = int(os.getenv("MAX_IMAGE_BYTES", str(10 * 1024 * 1024)))  # 10 MB
    ALLOWED_MIME: set = {"image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/webp"}

settings = Settings()
os.makedirs(settings.MEDIA_ROOT, exist_ok=True)
PHOTOS_DIR = os.path.join(settings.MEDIA_ROOT, "photos")
os.makedirs(PHOTOS_DIR, exist_ok=True)

# -------------------- DB Setup --------------------

Base = declarative_base()
engine = create_engine(
    settings.DATABASE_URL,
    connect_args={"check_same_thread": False} if "sqlite" in settings.DATABASE_URL else {},
)
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)

class Photo(Base):
    __tablename__ = "photos"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    name = Column(String(255), index=True, nullable=False)
    description = Column(String(1024), nullable=True)
    price = Column(Float, nullable=False)
    image_path = Column(String(1024), nullable=False)
    status = Column(String(32), index=True, nullable=False, default="active")  # active|pending|deleted
    created_at = Column(DateTime, nullable=False, default=datetime.utcnow)

    __table_args__ = (
        Index("idx_name_status", "name", "status"),
    )

Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

# -------------------- FastAPI App --------------------

app = FastAPI(title="Photo Catalog Backend", version="1.1.0")

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

# Serve media files at /media
app.mount("/media", StaticFiles(directory=settings.MEDIA_ROOT), name="media")

# -------------------- Utils --------------------

def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

def ensure_admin(x_admin_token: Optional[str] = Header(None)) -> None:
    if x_admin_token != settings.ADMIN_TOKEN:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Admin token invalid or missing.")

def unique_filename(original_name: str) -> str:
    ext = ""
    if "." in (original_name or ""):
        ext = "." + original_name.split(".")[-1].lower()
    return f"{uuid.uuid4().hex}{ext}"

def photo_to_dict(photo: Photo) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    basename = os.path.basename(photo.image_path)
    url = f"/media/photos/{basename}"
    return {
        "id": photo.id,
        "name": photo.name,
        "description": photo.description,
        "price": photo.price,
        "image_url": url,
        "status": photo.status,
        "created_at": photo.created_at.isoformat(),
    }

def delete_file_safely(path: str) -> None:
    try:
        if path and os.path.exists(path) and os.path.isfile(path):
            os.remove(path)
    except Exception:
        pass

def ensure_allowed_image(upload: UploadFile) -> None:
    if upload.content_type not in settings.ALLOWED_MIME:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=415,
            detail=f"Unsupported image type. Allowed: {sorted(settings.ALLOWED_MIME)}",
        )

# -------------------- Schemas --------------------

class ConflictCandidate(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    description: Optional[str]
    price: float
    image_url: str
    status: str
    created_at: str

class ConflictGroup(BaseModel):
    name: str
    active: Optional[ConflictCandidate] = None
    pending: List[ConflictCandidate]

class ResolveRequest(BaseModel):
    name: str
    keep_id: int

class ComparisonRow(BaseModel):
    rank: int
    id: int
    name: str
    price: float
    description: Optional[str]
    image_url: str
    tie_with_prev: bool

# -------------------- Routes --------------------

@app.post("/photos/submit")
async def submit_photo(
    name: str = Form(...),
    price: float = Form(...),
    description: Optional[str] = Form(None),
    image: UploadFile = File(...),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    # Validate fields
    name = (name or "").strip()
    if not name:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="Name cannot be empty.")
    try:
        price_val = float(price)
    except Exception:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="Price must be numeric.")
    if price_val < 0:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="Price cannot be negative.")

    ensure_allowed_image(image)

    # Store image to disk with a size guard
    safe_name = unique_filename(image.filename or "upload.bin")
    dest_path = os.path.join(PHOTOS_DIR, safe_name)

    total = 0
    try:
        with open(dest_path, "wb") as f:
            while True:
                chunk = await image.read(1024 * 256)
                if not chunk:
                    break
                total += len(chunk)
                if total > settings.MAX_IMAGE_BYTES:
                    raise HTTPException(status_code=413, detail="Image too large.")
                f.write(chunk)
    except HTTPException:
        delete_file_safely(dest_path)
        raise
    except Exception as e:
        delete_file_safely(dest_path)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Failed to save image: {e}")

    # Determine status; if an active photo with same name exists, mark as pending
    existing_active = db.execute(
        select(Photo).where(Photo.name == name, Photo.status == "active")
    ).scalar_one_or_none()
    status = "pending" if existing_active else "active"

    new_photo = Photo(
        name=name,
        description=(description or "").strip() or None,
        price=price_val,
        image_path=dest_path,
        status=status,
        created_at=datetime.utcnow(),
    )
    db.add(new_photo)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(new_photo)

    return {
        "message": "Submitted successfully." + (" Awaiting admin review due to duplicate name." if status == "pending" else ""),
        "photo": photo_to_dict(new_photo),
    }

@app.get("/photos")
def list_photos(
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
    q: Optional[str] = Query(None, description="Search term for name/description"),
    limit: int = Query(100, ge=1, le=500),
    offset: int = Query(0, ge=0),
):
    # Only active photos are visible to users
    stmt = select(Photo).where(Photo.status == "active")

    if q:
        q_norm = f"%{q.strip().lower()}%"
        stmt = stmt.where(
            func.lower(Photo.name).like(q_norm) |
            func.lower(func.coalesce(Photo.description, "")).like(q_norm)
        )

    # Sort ascending by (price, name, description). created_at for stable tie-break
    stmt = stmt.order_by(
        Photo.price.asc(),
        Photo.name.asc(),
        func.coalesce(Photo.description, "").asc(),
        Photo.created_at.asc(),
    ).limit(limit).offset(offset)

    photos = list(db.execute(stmt).scalars().all())
    return {
        "sorted_by": ["price", "name", "description"],
        "count": len(photos),
        "results": [photo_to_dict(p) for p in photos],
    }

@app.get("/photos/comparison", response_model=List[ComparisonRow])
def comparison(
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
    q: Optional[str] = Query(None, description="Optional search term to filter before comparison"),
    limit: int = Query(500, ge=1, le=2000),
    offset: int = Query(0, ge=0),
):
    # Build the same base set as list_photos (active only, optional search)
    stmt = select(Photo).where(Photo.status == "active")
    if q:
        q_norm = f"%{q.strip().lower()}%"
        stmt = stmt.where(
            func.lower(Photo.name).like(q_norm) |
            func.lower(func.coalesce(Photo.description, "")).like(q_norm)
        )

    # Primary comparison order: price ASC, name ASC, description ASC
    stmt = stmt.order_by(
        Photo.price.asc(),
        Photo.name.asc(),
        func.coalesce(Photo.description, "").asc(),
        Photo.created_at.asc(),
    ).limit(limit).offset(offset)

    rows = list(db.execute(stmt).scalars().all())

    # Build comparison rows with rank and tie flag relative to previous item
    result: List[ComparisonRow] = []
    prev_key = None
    for idx, p in enumerate(rows, start=1):
        key = (p.price, p.name, (p.description or ""))
        tie = (key == prev_key) if prev_key is not None else False
        prev_key = key
        d = photo_to_dict(p)
        result.append(ComparisonRow(
            rank=idx,
            id=d["id"],
            name=d["name"],
            price=d["price"],
            description=d["description"],
            image_url=d["image_url"],
            tie_with_prev=tie,
        ))
    return result

@app.get("/photos/conflicts", response_model=List[ConflictGroup], dependencies=[Depends(ensure_admin)])
def get_conflicts(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    # Find names with more than one entry or any pending entries
    names_multi = db.execute(select(Photo.name).group_by(Photo.name).having(func.count(Photo.id) > 1)).scalars().all()
    names_pending = db.execute(select(Photo.name).where(Photo.status == "pending").group_by(Photo.name)).scalars().all()
    conflict_names = sorted(set(names_multi) | set(names_pending))

    groups: List[ConflictGroup] = []
    for nm in conflict_names:
        items = db.execute(select(Photo).where(Photo.name == nm).order_by(Photo.created_at.asc())).scalars().all()
        active = next((i for i in items if i.status == "active"), None)
        pending = [i for i in items if i.status == "pending"]
        def as_cand(ph: Optional[Photo]):
            if not ph:
                return None
            d = photo_to_dict(ph)
            return ConflictCandidate(**d)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        groups.append(ConflictGroup(
            name=nm,
            active=as_cand(active),
            pending=[ConflictCandidate(**photo_to_dict(p)) for p in pending],
        ))
    return groups

@app.post("/photos/conflicts/resolve", dependencies=[Depends(ensure_admin)])
def resolve_conflict(body: ResolveRequest, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    # Fetch all photos with this name
    items = db.execute(select(Photo).where(Photo.name == body.name)).scalars().all()
    if not items:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="No photos found for this name.")

    keep = next((i for i in items if i.id == body.keep_id), None)
    if not keep:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="keep_id does not belong to the specified name.")

    # Mark the chosen one as active; delete others (file + DB)
    for it in items:
        if it.id == keep.id:
            it.status = "active"
        else:
            # remove file and row
            delete_file_safely(it.image_path)
            db.delete(it)
    db.commit()

    # Enforce invariant: only one active photo per name remains
    return {"message": "Conflict resolved.", "kept": photo_to_dict(keep)}
```

Can you discuss potential limitations or challenges in developing the forecasting tool and suggest ways to address them?

Here are the key limitations and challenges when developing the forecasting tool, with concrete mitigations you can apply directly to the scaffold you’re building:

1) Label noise and ground truth alignment
- Challenge: Mapping statements to the correct meeting cutoff without look-ahead; inconsistent labels for hike/hold/cut across data vendors and eras (target range vs target rate).
- Mitigations:
  - Enforce strict time windows: include only documents released before the decision timestamp; unit test window logic.
  - Normalize labels from target_rate_bps and prev_target_rate_bps to derive hike/hold/cut deterministically.
  - Deduplicate sources by content hash and canonicalize text (lowercasing, unicode fixups).

2) Regime shifts and structural breaks
- Challenge: Lexicon relationships drift (e.g., “transitory” flipped in meaning); policy frameworks change (QE/QT, average inflation targeting).
- Mitigations:
  - Implement rolling/expanding z-scores and Page–Hinkley (or CUSUM) tests; when a break is detected, re-fit calibration on a recent window.
  - Date-stamp lexicon versions; allow per-era overrides and bank-specific terms.

3) Model miscalibration of probabilities
- Challenge: Linear HDS→probability mapping is interpretable but often miscalibrated.
- Mitigations:
  - Fit isotonic or logistic calibration on out-of-sample folds; clip probabilities to [1e-4, 1 - 1e-4]; monitor reliability diagrams and Brier loss.
  - Pool with priors via linear pooling to avoid overconfident extremes in sparse regimes.

4) Data sparsity and document heterogeneity
- Challenge: FOMC statements are infrequent; minutes, speeches, and press conferences have different signal strengths; some meetings have no pre-cutoff documents.
- Mitigations:
  - Weight by doc_type (e.g., statement=1.0, press_conf=0.9, minutes=0.8, speech=0.6); backfill with rolling means (7d/30d) and last-observation-carried-forward.
  - Use hierarchical pooling across doc types and meetings; fall back to prior-only probabilities when no signal exists.

5) Lexicon brittleness and context/negation issues
- Challenge: Bag-of-words misses context, sarcasm, or multiword expressions; naive negation scope can invert meaning incorrectly.
- Mitigations:
  - Maintain a domain lexicon with bigrams/phrases (e.g., “higher for longer”); expand negation scope tests and add intensifier handling.
  - Benchmark against TF-IDF, transformer embeddings, or supervised classifiers trained on labeled Fed text; keep lexicon scorer as a transparent baseline.

6) Look-ahead and data leakage
- Challenge: Accidentally using statements or market data published after the decision time contaminates backtests.
- Mitigations:
  - Enforce cutoff timestamps; write assertions to reject any post-cutoff text.
  - Use walk-forward splits (time-based CV) only; no random shuffles.

7) Evaluation pitfalls
- Challenge: Class imbalance (holds dominate), unstable metrics across eras, overlapping windows inflate sample size.
- Mitigations:
  - Report Brier score and classwise Brier, macro-averaged; compute expected calibration error; bootstrap confidence intervals.
  - Ensure independence by evaluating at the meeting level (one forecast per meeting).

8) Mapping tone to yields vs policy probabilities
- Challenge: The relationship between hawkish tone and yields varies by term premium and macro regime; an HDS→prob mapping may not translate linearly to yield changes.
- Mitigations:
  - Separate modules: (a) HDS→policy probabilities; (b) probabilities→expected path of short rates; (c) term-structure bridge (e.g., simple expectations hypothesis plus term-premium proxy) to map to 1y/2y yields.
  - Recalibrate yield mapping per era and validate with event-studies around statement timestamps.

9) Cross-bank and cross-era comparability
- Challenge: Different central banks use different language conventions; the Fed’s tone in 2001 isn’t directly comparable to 2021.
- Mitigations:
  - Bank-specific lexicons and calibrations; rolling standardization (expanding z-scores) within bank and doc type.
  - When aggregating 25 years, use year- or regime-specific intercepts in calibration models.

10) Text acquisition, OCR, and scraping quality
- Challenge: Historical PDFs, OCR noise, website changes; missing or corrupted documents.
- Mitigations:
  - Store raw + normalized text; track provenance and checksums; implement retry and duplicate detection.
  - Use robust tokenization and aggressive whitespace/unicode normalization; flag unusually short/long documents.

11) Uncertainty quantification
- Challenge: Small samples per regime make single-point probabilities misleading.
- Mitigations:
  - Bootstrap meetings to produce predictive intervals for probabilities; report median and 5–95% bands.
  - Use Bayesian calibration or conformal prediction for distribution-free coverage where feasible.

12) Governance and interpretability
- Challenge: Stakeholders require explainability for policy tools.
- Mitigations:
  - Log token-level contributions (top positive/negative words and phrases); version models, lexicons, and calibration artifacts; produce model cards and change logs.

By incorporating these safeguards—strict time cutoffs, regime detection, calibration, priors, doc-type weighting, robust data handling, and uncertainty estimates—you materially reduce overfitting and leakage risk while keeping the HDS mapping interpretable and operational over a 25-year Fed history.
Include methods for analyzing hawkish policy statements' impact on bond yields and discuss potential limitations or challenges in developing the forecasting tool.

```python
# hawkish_yield_impact_toolkit.py
# Turn central-bank text into a Hawk-Dove Score (HDS), map to next-meeting rate
# probabilities, and estimate the 1-year government bond yield via an
# expectations-based bridge. Includes an event-study regression utility to
# quantify how yield changes co-move with HDS or probability shocks.
#
# Mapping rule (per spec):
#   +10 HDS => +10 percentage points probability of a hike at the next meeting
#   -10 HDS => +10 percentage points probability of a cut at the next meeting

import re
import math
import datetime as dt
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Dict, Optional, Tuple


# --------------------------
# Data containers
# --------------------------

@dataclass
class Statement:
    date: dt.datetime
    text: str
    bank: str = "Unknown"
    meta: Optional[Dict] = None


@dataclass
class ScoredStatement:
    date: dt.datetime
    raw: float     # per-100-token raw score (positive = hawkish)
    z: float       # expanding z-score vs prior samples
    hds: float     # Hawk-Dove Score in [-100, 100]
    bank: str = "Unknown"
    meta: Optional[Dict] = None


@dataclass
class Meeting:
    meeting_id: str
    end: dt.datetime        # decision/cutoff timestamp (UTC or consistent TZ)
    bank: str = "Unknown"


# --------------------------
# Utilities
# --------------------------

def _to_datetime_utc(x) -> dt.datetime:
    if isinstance(x, dt.datetime):
        return x if x.tzinfo else x.replace(tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)
    if isinstance(x, dt.date):
        return dt.datetime(x.year, x.month, x.day, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)
    s = str(x).strip().replace("Z", "")
    if "T" in s or ":" in s:
        y, m, d = int(s[0:4]), int(s[5:7]), int(s[8:10])
        hh = int(s[11:13]) if len(s) >= 13 else 0
        mm = int(s[14:16]) if len(s) >= 16 else 0
        ss = int(s[17:19]) if len(s) >= 19 else 0
        return dt.datetime(y, m, d, hh, mm, ss, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)
    y, m, d = map(int, s.split("-"))
    return dt.datetime(y, m, d, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)


def _dcf(t0: dt.datetime, t1: dt.datetime) -> float:
    # Act/365 fraction; clip at zero
    return max(0.0, (t1 - t0).total_seconds()) / (365.0 * 24.0 * 3600.0)


# --------------------------
# Scorer: lexicon + negation + intensifiers
# --------------------------

class HawkDoveScorer:
    """
    Produces:
      - raw score (per 100 tokens; positive = hawkish)
      - z-score (expanding vs prior samples, to avoid look-ahead)
      - HDS = 100 * tanh(z / scale) in [-100, 100]
    """

    def __init__(self, z_to_score_scale: float = 2.0):
        self.z_to_score_scale = z_to_score_scale
        self.lex = self._default_lexicon()
        self.negators = {"not", "no", "never", "neither", "nor", "hardly", "rarely", "seldom", "without", "unlikely", "less"}
        self.intensifiers = {
            "very": 1.3, "significantly": 1.5, "substantially": 1.5, "considerably": 1.4,
            "clearly": 1.2, "materially": 1.3, "persistently": 1.3, "strongly": 1.3, "elevated": 1.2
        }
        self.bigram_weights = {
            ("higher", "for"): 0.25,  # "higher for longer" motif
            ("for", "longer"): 0.25,
            ("further", "tightening"): 0.5,
            ("restrictive", "stance"): 0.3,
            ("rate", "cuts"): -0.6,
            ("rate", "reduction"): -0.6
        }

    def _default_lexicon(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        # Positive = hawkish; Negative = dovish. Extend for your bank/era.
        return {
            "inflation": 0.5, "elevated": 0.4, "tighten": 1.0, "tightening": 1.0,
            "raise": 0.7, "hike": 0.8, "restrictive": 0.9, "robust": 0.4, "strong": 0.3,
            "persistence": 0.3, "upside": 0.3, "pressures": 0.2, "vigilant": 0.4, "overheating": 0.6,
            "accommodative": -0.9, "stimulus": -0.6, "easing": -1.0, "ease": -0.8,
            "cut": -0.8, "lower": -0.5, "downside": -0.3, "weakness": -0.3, "softening": -0.3,
            "recession": -0.4, "slack": -0.3
        }

    def _tokens(self, text: str) -> List[str]:
        return re.findall(r"[a-z']+", (text or "").lower().replace("\u2019", "'"))

    def score_text_raw(self, text: str, neg_scope: int = 3) -> float:
        """
        Return raw score per 100 tokens, with simple negation/intensifier handling.
        """
        toks = self._tokens(text)
        n = max(1, len(toks))
        score = 0.0

        # Unigram with context
        for i, w in enumerate(toks):
            base = self.lex.get(w, 0.0)
            if base == 0.0:
                continue
            # Negation scope over preceding neg_scope tokens
            neg = any(toks[j] in self.negators for j in range(max(0, i - neg_scope), i))
            sgn = -1.0 if neg else 1.0
            # Intensifier if previous token is in dictionary
            scale = self.intensifiers.get(toks[i - 1], 1.0) if i > 0 else 1.0
            score += sgn * scale * base

        # Lightweight bigram nudge
        for i in range(len(toks) - 1):
            score += self.bigram_weights.get((toks[i], toks[i + 1]), 0.0)

        return 100.0 * score / n

    def series_to_scores(self, statements: List[Statement]) -> List[ScoredStatement]:
        """
        Sequentially compute raw -> expanding z -> HDS without look-ahead.
        """
        out: List[ScoredStatement] = []
        raws: List[float] = []
        for i, s in enumerate(sorted(statements, key=lambda x: x.date)):
            r = self.score_text_raw(s.text)
            if i == 0:
                mu, sd = 0.0, 1.0
            else:
                mu = sum(raws) / len(raws)
                var = sum((x - mu) ** 2 for x in raws) / max(1, len(raws) - 1)
                sd = math.sqrt(var) if var > 1e-12 else 1.0
            z = (r - mu) / sd
            hds = 100.0 * math.tanh(z / max(1e-6, self.z_to_score_scale))
            out.append(ScoredStatement(date=s.date, raw=r, z=z, hds=hds, bank=s.bank, meta=s.meta))
            raws.append(r)
        return out


# --------------------------
# Probabilities and pooling
# --------------------------

def signal_probabilities_from_hds(hds: float) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """
    Mapping per spec:
      +10 HDS => +10% probability of a hike
      -10 HDS => +10% probability of a cut
    """
    p_hike = max(hds, 0.0) / 100.0
    p_cut = max(-hds, 0.0) / 100.0
    p_hold = max(0.0, 1.0 - p_hike - p_cut)
    s = p_hike + p_hold + p_cut
    if s <= 0:
        return {"p_hike": 1/3, "p_hold": 1/3, "p_cut": 1/3}
    return {"p_hike": p_hike / s, "p_hold": p_hold / s, "p_cut": p_cut / s}


def linear_pool(signal_probs: Dict[str, float],
                prior_probs: Optional[Dict[str, float]],
                weight_signal: float = 0.5) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """
    Pooled = w * signal + (1 - w) * prior
    """
    prior = prior_probs or {"p_hike": 1/3, "p_hold": 1/3, "p_cut": 1/3}
    w = min(1.0, max(0.0, weight_signal))
    out = {
        k: w * signal_probs.get(k, 0.0) + (1 - w) * prior.get(k, 0.0)
        for k in ("p_hike", "p_hold", "p_cut")
    }
    s = sum(out.values())
    if s > 0:
        out = {k: v / s for k, v in out.items()}
    return out


# --------------------------
# Expectations-based yield bridge
# --------------------------

def expected_1y_yield_from_probs(current_rate: float,
                                 probs: Dict[str, float],
                                 hike_size_bps: float = 25.0,
                                 cut_size_bps: float = 25.0,
                                 term_premium_bps: float = 0.0) -> float:
    """
    Approximate 1Y yield as: expected average policy rate over next year + term premium.
    Very simple path: one potential move at next meeting by fixed step.

    Inputs are in percent for rates; bps for step sizes/premium.
    Returns percent.
    """
    p_hike, p_hold, p_cut = probs["p_hike"], probs["p_hold"], probs["p_cut"]]
    step_up = hike_size_bps / 10000.0
    step_dn = cut_size_bps / 10000.0
    next_rate = (
        p_hike * (current_rate + step_up) +
        p_hold * current_rate +
        p_cut  * (current_rate - step_dn)
    )
    # Simple 1Y average: assume move happens near-term and then held
    exp_avg = next_rate
    return 100.0 * exp_avg + term_premium_bps / 100.0


def yield_impact_vs_prior(current_rate: float,
                          prior_probs: Dict[str, float],
                          signal_probs: Dict[str, float],
                          weight_signal: float = 0.5,
                          hike_size_bps: float = 25.0,
                          cut_size_bps: float = 25.0,
                          term_premium_bps: float = 0.0) -> float:
    """
    Return the change in model 1Y yield (in percentage points) when
    incorporating the signal vs prior-only baseline.
    """
    pooled = linear_pool(signal_probs, prior_probs, weight_signal)
    y_pooled = expected_1y_yield_from_probs(current_rate, pooled, hike_size_bps, cut_size_bps, term_premium_bps)
    y_prior = expected_1y_yield_from_probs(current_rate, prior_probs, hike_size_bps, cut_size_bps, term_premium_bps)
    return y_pooled - y_prior


# --------------------------
# Event-study regression utility (impact of HDS on yields)
# --------------------------

def event_study_regression(events: List[Tuple[dt.datetime, float]],
                           yield_changes_bps: List[float]) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """
    Simple OLS without external deps: dY_bps = alpha + beta * HDS + eps
    Returns (alpha, beta). Inputs:
      - events: list of (timestamp, HDS) for statement windows
      - yield_changes_bps: parallel list of 1Y (or 2Y/5Y) yield changes in bps in a narrow window
    """
    assert len(events) == len(yield_changes_bps) and len(events) > 1
    x = [hds for (_, hds) in events]
    y = yield_changes_bps
    n = len(x)
    xbar = sum(x) / n
    ybar = sum(y) / n
    sxx = sum((xi - xbar) ** 2 for xi in x)
    sxy = sum((xi - xbar) * (yi - ybar) for xi, yi in zip(x, y))
    beta = sxy / sxx if sxx != 0 else 0.0
    alpha = ybar - beta * xbar
    return alpha, beta


# --------------------------
# End-to-end helper
# --------------------------

def hds_to_rate_hike_probability(hds: float,
                                 prior_probs: Optional[Dict[str, float]] = None,
                                 weight_signal: float = 0.5) -> Dict[str, float]:
    signal = signal_probabilities_from_hds(hds)
    return linear_pool(signal, prior_probs, weight_signal)


def analyze_statement_impact(statement_text: str,
                             current_rate_percent: float,
                             prior_probs: Dict[str, float],
                             weight_signal: float = 0.5,
                             hike_size_bps: float = 25.0,
                             cut_size_bps: float = 25.0,
                             term_premium_bps: float = 0.0) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """
    Score a single statement, compute probabilities, and estimate yield impact.
    Returns dict with HDS, pooled probabilities, and yield impact (pct-pts and bps).
    """
    scorer = HawkDoveScorer()
    hds = scorer.score_text_raw(statement_text)  # raw per-100-token score as quick proxy
    # Map raw->z->HDS would require a history; for one-off we squash raw via tanh
    hds = 100.0 * math.tanh(hds / 10.0)
    signal = signal_probabilities_from_hds(hds)
    pooled = linear_pool(signal, prior_probs, weight_signal)
    dy_pct = yield_impact_vs_prior(current_rate_percent / 100.0, prior_probs, signal,
                                   weight_signal, hike_size_bps, cut_size_bps, term_premium_bps)
    return {
        "HDS": hds,
        "signal_probs": signal,
        "pooled_probs": pooled,
        "yield_impact_pct_pts": dy_pct,
        "yield_impact_bps": dy_pct * 100.0
    }
```

Key ideas and formulas
- Piecewise-constant hazard: for time t in interval k = (c_{k-1}, c_k], hazard λ_k(x) = exp(β0_k + β_age*age + β_sex*sex), where β0_k are interval baselines, and β_age, β_sex are common across intervals.
- Conditional survival after a landmark L:
  S(u | T ≥ L, x) = exp(-∫_{L}^{L+u} λ(s | x) ds), with λ(s|x) constant within each interval. This makes the integral a sum of λ_k(x) times the overlap lengths with each interval after L.
- Expected remaining lifetime given survival to L:
  E[T − L | T ≥ L, x] = ∫_{0}^{∞} S(u | T ≥ L, x) du
  Under piecewise-constant hazard, this integral is a sum of exponential tail integrals across intervals.

We will implement E[T − L | T ≥ L, x] by stepping through intervals after L and summing:
- For each interval segment j after L, with hazard h_j and segment length d_j:
  Contribution = S_cum * (1 − exp(−h_j d_j)) / h_j
  Update S_cum <- S_cum * exp(−h_j d_j)
- For the last open-ended interval (if Inf), contribution = S_cum / h_last

```r
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)

# Piecewise-constant hazard intervals (in months)
cuts <- c(0, 3, 6, 12, 24, Inf)

# Helper: ensure 'sex' factor has 'male','female' levels as specified
# df is assumed to exist with columns: id, start, stop, event, age, sex

#-----------------------------------------------
# 2) Expand data to piecewise intervals (Poisson)
#-----------------------------------------------
# We'll create one row per subject per interval they are at risk in.
# Each row has: exposure time within the interval and event indicator if event occurs in that interval.

# Function to cut a [start, stop) into the piecewise intervals
split_to_intervals <- function(start, stop, cuts_vec) {
  # For infinite last cut, handle by a large value but we will clip to stop anyway
  finite_cuts <- cuts_vec
  # Determine interval bounds that overlap [start, stop)
  lefts  <- head(finite_cuts, -1)
  rights <- tail(finite_cuts, -1)
  # Overlap with [start, stop)
  int_start <- pmax(lefts, start)
  int_stop  <- pmin(rights, stop)
  keep <- int_stop > int_start
  tibble(
    int_left = lefts[keep],
    int_right = rights[keep],
    seg_start = int_start[keep],
    seg_stop  = int_stop[keep]
  )
}

# Build interval-level dataset
df_pw <- df %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(.intervals = list(split_to_intervals(start, stop, cuts))) %>%
  unnest(.intervals) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    exposure = pmax(0, seg_stop - seg_start),
    # Event occurs in the last segment if stop is event and seg_stop == stop
    y = as.integer(event == 1 & seg_stop == stop),
    # Interval factor (strata) based on the piece boundaries
    int_stratum = factor(paste0("(", int_left, ",", int_right, "]"),
                         levels = paste0("(", head(cuts, -1), ",", tail(cuts, -1), "]"))
  )

# Sanity: no negative exposures
stopifnot(all(df_pw$exposure >= 0))

#-------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Fit stratified Poisson (piecewise exponential) GLM
#-------------------------------------------------------
# We fit a Poisson GLM with:
# - outcome: y (events)
# - offset: log(exposure)
# - predictors: age, sex
# - strata-specific intercepts: implemented via factor(int_stratum) with no global intercept
# This yields one baseline log-rate per interval, plus covariate effects shared across intervals.

# Make sure exposures > 0 for Poisson fit (drop zero-exposure rows, which shouldn't happen but safe-guard)
df_fit <- df_pw %>% filter(exposure > 0)

fit <- glm(
  y ~ 0 + int_stratum + age + sex,   # 0 removes global intercept so each stratum gets its own baseline
  family = poisson(),
  offset = log(exposure),
  data = df_fit
)

summary(fit)

# Extract fitted coefficients
coefs <- broom::tidy(fit)
coefs

# Build a function that returns the hazard rate for a given interval and covariates
# Hazard h_k(x) = exp(β0_k + β_age*age + β_sexfemale*I(sex=='female')) since 'sex' is a factor
get_interval_hazard <- function(int_left, int_right, age, sex, fit_obj) {
  # Build a newdata design row for predict
  int_label <- paste0("(", int_left, ",", int_right, "]")
  nd <- tibble(
    int_stratum = factor(int_label,
                         levels = paste0("(", head(cuts, -1), ",", tail(cuts, -1), "]")),
    age = age,
    sex = factor(sex, levels = levels(df$sex))
  )
  # For Poisson with log link and offset=0, the linear predictor is log(rate).
  # We'll set exposure=1 so offset=log(1)=0 for prediction.
  pred <- predict(fit_obj, newdata = nd, type = "link", se.fit = FALSE)
  # Hazard is rate per unit time within the interval (same as Poisson rate)
  h <- as.numeric(exp(pred))
  return(h)
}

#-------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Identify alive patients and their landmark times (L_i)
#-------------------------------------------------------------
# We interpret "still alive" as those with event==0 at their last observed stop.
# For each id, take their latest record; if event==0, they are alive at L_i = stop (current observed time).

last_obs <- df %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = stop, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

alive <- last_obs %>%
  filter(event == 0) %>%
  transmute(id, L = stop, age = age, sex = sex)

#-------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) For each alive patient, compute E[T-L | T >= L, x]
#-------------------------------------------------------------
# We step through the piecewise intervals after L, multiplying survival across segments,
# and summing expected contributions. If L lies inside an interval, that interval's remaining
# portion is the first segment. Then follow full intervals up to Inf.
#
# For each segment j with hazard h_j and segment length d_j:
#  - survival entering segment: S_cum
#  - contribution to mean residual life: (S_cum * (1 - exp(-h_j * d_j))) / h_j
#  - update S_cum <- S_cum * exp(-h_j * d_j)
# For the last open-ended interval (ending at Inf): add S_cum / h_last and stop.

# Build a reusable per-patient function
expected_remaining_life_pwch <- function(L, age, sex, cuts_vec, fit_obj) {
  lefts  <- head(cuts_vec, -1)
  rights <- tail(cuts_vec, -1)

  # Identify intervals at/after L
  # Segment j: overlap of (max(L, left), right)
  # Start with the interval containing L (if L equals a cut, we start at the next interval)
  # We'll treat segments only where right > max(L, left).

  S_cum <- 1.0
  mrl <- 0.0  # mean residual life accumulator

  for (k in seq_along(lefts)) {
    a <- lefts[k]
    b <- rights[k]

    # Determine segment after L
    seg_start <- max(L, a)
    seg_end   <- b

    # If L >= b, no overlap (this interval ends before or at L)
    if (seg_end <= seg_start) next

    # Segment duration: if b is Inf, we mark as open-ended
    if (is.infinite(b)) {
      # Hazard in this last open-ended interval
      h <- get_interval_hazard(a, b, age, sex, fit_obj)
      # Add infinite tail: S_cum / h
      mrl <- mrl + S_cum / h
      # No further intervals
      return(mrl)
    } else {
      d <- seg_end - seg_start
      h <- get_interval_hazard(a, b, age, sex, fit_obj)
      if (h <= 0) {
        # Numerical guard (shouldn't happen with Poisson/exp)
        # If h ~ 0, survival ~ 1 and contribution ~ S_cum * d
        mrl <- mrl + S_cum * d
      } else {
        mrl <- mrl + S_cum * (1 - exp(-h * d)) / h
        S_cum <- S_cum * exp(-h * d)
      }
    }
  }

  # If we exit the loop without hitting Inf, add nothing more (no tail). This can happen if cuts do not include Inf.
  return(mrl)
}

# Vectorized application to all alive patients
alive_mrl <- alive %>%
  mutate(
    mrl = pmap_dbl(list(L, age, sex),
                   ~ expected_remaining_life_pwch(L = ..1, age = ..2, sex = ..3,
                                                  cuts_vec = cuts, fit_obj = fit))
  )

#-------------------------------------------------------------
# Build a small function to get S(u | T>=L, x) at a vector of u >= 0
cond_surv_curve <- function(u_vec, L, age, sex, cuts_vec, fit_obj) {
  # For each u, compute cumulative hazard from L to L+u and exponentiate
  # Efficient approach: walk intervals and accumulate piecewise.
  lefts  <- head(cuts_vec, -1)
  rights <- tail(cuts_vec, -1)

  # Sort u
  u_order <- order(u_vec)
  u_sorted <- u_vec[u_order]

  S_out <- numeric(length(u_sorted))
  H_cum <- 0.0
  u_cursor <- 0.0
  t_cursor <- L

  for (k in seq_along(lefts)) {
    a <- lefts[k]; b <- rights[k]
    seg_start <- max(L, a)
    if (b <= seg_start) next

    h <- get_interval_hazard(a, b, age, sex, fit_obj)

    # We will fill S(u) for u where L+u lies within [seg_start, b)
    while (TRUE) {
      # Next time boundary in absolute time
      t_boundary <- b
      # Next u boundary we can fill up to
      u_boundary <- t_boundary - L

      # Indices of u that fall in [max(u_cursor, seg_start-L), u_boundary)
      u_low <- max(u_cursor, seg_start - L)
      idx <- which(u_sorted >= u_low & u_sorted < u_boundary)
      if (length(idx) > 0) {
        # For these u, additional time since last filled is du = u - u_cursor
        du <- u_sorted[idx] - u_cursor
        H_cum_here <- H_cum + h * du
        S_out[idx] <- exp(-H_cum_here)
      }

      # Advance to next segment or finish if no more u in this segment
      # Update cumulative hazard up to u_boundary if we will move on
      if (any(u_sorted >= u_boundary)) {
        # Move to next interval
        dseg <- u_boundary - u_cursor
        if (dseg > 0) H_cum <- H_cum + h * dseg
        u_cursor <- u_boundary
        break
      } else {
        # All remaining u are before next boundary; we are done
        break
      }
    }

    # Continue to next interval if needed
  }

  # For any remaining u beyond last finite cut (i.e., in Inf interval)
  if (any(is.infinite(rights))) {
    # Last interval is (a_inf, Inf)
    a_inf <- tail(lefts, 1)
    h_last <- get_interval_hazard(a_inf, Inf, age, sex, fit_obj)
    # Fill remaining u >= u_cursor
    rem_idx <- which(u_sorted >= u_cursor)
    if (length(rem_idx) > 0) {
      du <- u_sorted[rem_idx] - u_cursor
      H_cum_here <- H_cum + h_last * du
      S_out[rem_idx] <- exp(-H_cum_here)
    }
  }

  # Reorder back
  out <- numeric(length(u_vec))
  out[u_order] <- S_out
  out
}
```

Explanation of key steps
- Data expansion: We split each [start, stop) into the user-defined intervals (cuts). For each overlapping interval, we compute the exposure (time at risk) and whether the event occurred in that interval. This yields a dataset suitable for a Poisson GLM that is equivalent to a piecewise exponential survival model.
- Model fitting: We fit y ~ 0 + int_stratum + age + sex with Poisson family and offset log(exposure). Each interval gets its own baseline log-rate (int_stratum), while age and sex have common effects on the log-hazard. The fitted linear predictor equals log(hazard) within an interval for a given age/sex.
- Conditional mean residual life (MRL): For each alive patient with landmark L, we walk intervals that occur after L. In each segment, with hazard h and length d:
  - The survival entering the segment is S_cum.
  - The expected time contributed within that segment before failure or end-of-segment is S_cum * (1 − e^(−h d)) / h.
  - Survival is then reduced by e^(−h d).
  For the final open-ended interval, the tail expectation is S_cum / h_last. Summing these gives E[T − L | T ≥ L, x].
- Averaging: We average per-patient MRL across all alive patients to obtain the average additional survival time for the alive cohort. If you want to weight patients differently, you can compute a weighted mean of mrl with your desired weights.

# Piecewise constant hazard (piecewise exponential) model in R
# - Intervals: [0,3), [3,6), [6,12), [12, Inf)
# - Data: df with time, status (1=death, 0=censor), age (numeric), gender (factor: female,male)

# - We:

#   3) Alternatively fit a stratified Cox model by interval and compare

# -----------------------------
# 0) Setup and example data
# -----------------------------
set.seed(123)

if (!exists("df")) {
  n <- 600
  # Covariates
  age <- round(rnorm(n, mean = 65, sd = 10), 1)
  gender <- factor(sample(c("female", "male"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.5, 0.5)),
                   levels = c("female", "male"))

  # True piecewise baseline hazards per interval (for simulation)
  # Intervals: [0,3), [3,6), [6,12), [12, Inf)
  cuts <- c(0, 3, 6, 12, Inf)
  base_h <- c(0.12, 0.08, 0.05, 0.03)  # per month hazards (example)
  # Log-HR for age (per year) and male vs female
  beta_age <- log(1.02)         # ~2% ↑ per year
  beta_male <- log(1.25)        # 25% ↑ for male

  # Simulate piecewise exponential survival times
  # For each subject, traverse intervals and sample exponential waiting times
  sim_times <- numeric(n)
  sim_event <- integer(n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    xb <- beta_age * age[i] + beta_male * (gender[i] == "male")
    t <- 0
    ev <- 0
    for (k in 1:4) {
      hk <- base_h[k] * exp(xb)
      if (is.infinite(cuts[k + 1])) {
        # Last interval
        wait <- rexp(1, rate = hk)
        t <- t + wait
        ev <- 1
        break
      } else {
        width <- cuts[k + 1] - max(t, cuts[k])
        # If entering interval before its start, align to the start
        if (t < cuts[k]) t <- cuts[k]
        # Draw exponential and check if it occurs within this interval
        wait <- rexp(1, rate = hk)
        if (wait < (cuts[k + 1] - t)) {
          t <- t + wait
          ev <- 1
          break
        } else {
          # Survives through the interval
          t <- cuts[k + 1]
        }
      }
    }
    # Add independent right censoring (uniform between 9 and 18 months)
    cens <- runif(1, 9, 18)
    if (t > cens) {
      t <- cens
      ev <- 0
    }
    sim_times[i] <- t
    sim_event[i] <- ev
  }

  df <- data.frame(
    time = sim_times,
    status = sim_event,
    age = as.numeric(age),
    gender = factor(gender, levels = c("female", "male"))
  )

                   include.lowest = TRUE,

stopifnot(all(split_df$time >= split_df$tstart))

# -----------------------------
# 2) Fit piecewise exponential via Poisson regression
# -----------------------------
# Model: events ~ age + gender + interval (factor), offset(log(exposure))
# This is equivalent to a piecewise constant baseline hazard with interval-specific rates.
# Important: rows with zero exposure (if any) should be excluded
fit_pois <- glm(
  formula = status ~ age + gender + interval,
  family = poisson(),
  offset = log(exposure + 1e-12),  # tiny epsilon avoids log(0) if any zero exposure
  data = subset(split_df, exposure > 0)
)
summary(fit_pois)

# Extract interval-specific baseline log-hazards:
# In a Poisson model with log link: log(E[event]) = log(h) + log(exposure) + X*beta
# => log(h) = intercept + interval_k effect (with one interval as reference)
# We'll construct the hazard for each interval at reference levels (age=0, gender=female),
# and we will add covariate effects for individual predictions.
interval_levels <- levels(split_df$interval)
coef_all <- coef(fit_pois)
vcov_all <- vcov(fit_pois)

# Identify which coefficient is the intercept and the interval contrasts
intercept <- coef_all["(Intercept)"]
# Build vector of log-baseline hazards per interval (at reference covariates)
# Reference interval is the first level of 'interval' in the model matrix
# We will reconstruct each interval's log-baseline hazard as:
#   log h_k,0 = intercept + interval_k coefficient (0 for reference)
log_h0_by_interval <- setNames(numeric(length(interval_levels)), interval_levels)
for (k in seq_along(interval_levels)) {
  lev <- interval_levels[k]
  term_name <- paste0("interval", lev)
  add <- if (term_name %in% names(coef_all)) coef_all[term_name] else 0
  log_h0_by_interval[k] <- intercept + add
}
h0_by_interval <- exp(log_h0_by_interval)

h0_by_interval  # piecewise baseline hazards (per month) at age=0, gender=female

# -----------------------------
# 3) Alternative: Cox model stratified by interval
# -----------------------------
# The Cox model with strata(interval) allows different baseline hazards per interval,
# while sharing covariate effects (age, gender).
fit_cox <- coxph(Surv(tstart, time, status) ~ age + gender + strata(interval),
                 data = subset(split_df, exposure > 0))
summary(fit_cox)

exp(coef(fit_pois)[c("age", "gendermale")])  # Poisson HRs
exp(coef(fit_cox))                            # Cox HRs (age, gendermale)

# -----------------------------
# 4) Functions to get individual piecewise hazards and survival
# -----------------------------
# Given a subject's covariates x = (age, gender), the hazard in interval k is:
#   h_k(x) = h0_k * exp(beta_age*age + beta_male*I(male))
# We compute:
#   - piecewise hazards
#   - survival at any time t: S(t|x) = exp( - sum_k h_k(x) * width_k(t) )
# where width_k(t) is the time spent in interval k up to t.

# Extract covariate coefficients from Poisson fit
beta_age <- coef_all["age"]
beta_male <- if ("gendermale" %in% names(coef_all)) coef_all["gendermale"] else 0

# Convenience: get interval index for any time t
interval_index <- function(t, cuts) {
  # returns k in {1..K} such that t in [cuts[k], cuts[k+1))
  # t can be vector
  K <- length(cuts) - 1
  idx <- findInterval(t, vec = cuts, left.open = FALSE, rightmost.closed = FALSE, all.inside = FALSE)
  # findInterval with our right=FALSE labeling puts t==cuts[k] in interval k
  # Any t >= last finite cut goes to K
  idx[idx == 0] <- 1
  idx[idx > K] <- K
  return(idx)
}

# Compute piecewise hazard vector for one subject
hazard_piecewise <- function(age, gender, h0_by_interval, beta_age, beta_male) {
  xb <- beta_age * age + beta_male * as.numeric(gender == "male")
  as.numeric(h0_by_interval) * exp(xb)
}

# Cumulative hazard up to time t for one subject
cumhaz_piecewise <- function(t, age, gender, cuts, h0_by_interval, beta_age, beta_male) {
  hvec <- hazard_piecewise(age, gender, h0_by_interval, beta_age, beta_male)
  K <- length(hvec)
  # For each interval k, compute contribution: h_k * width_k(t)
  contrib <- numeric(K)
  for (k in seq_len(K)) {
    left <- cuts[k]
    right <- cuts[k + 1]
    width <- pmax(0, pmin(t, right) - left)
    contrib[k] <- hvec[k] * pmax(0, width)
  }
  sum(contrib)
}

# Survival at time t for one subject
S_piecewise <- function(t, age, gender, cuts, h0_by_interval, beta_age, beta_male) {
  H <- cumhaz_piecewise(t, age, gender, cuts, h0_by_interval, beta_age, beta_male)
  exp(-H)
}

# Vectorized survival over a grid
S_over_grid <- function(t_vec, age, gender, cuts, h0_by_interval, beta_age, beta_male) {
  sapply(t_vec, function(tt) S_piecewise(tt, age, gender, cuts, h0_by_interval, beta_age, beta_male))
}

# -----------------------------
# 5) Mean residual life (MRL) at landmark t0
# -----------------------------
# Definition:
#  MRL(t0 | x) = E[T - t0 | T > t0, x] = ∫_{t0}^{∞} S(u|x) / S(t0|x) du
# For piecewise-constant hazards, this integral has a closed-form sum of exponentials.
# We implement a closed-form evaluator.

mrl_piecewise <- function(t0, age, gender, cuts, h0_by_interval, beta_age, beta_male) {
  hvec <- hazard_piecewise(age, gender, h0_by_interval, beta_age, beta_male)
  K <- length(hvec)
  # Identify the current interval at t0
  k0 <- interval_index(t0, cuts)
  # Survival at t0
  S_t0 <- S_piecewise(t0, age, gender, cuts, h0_by_interval, beta_age, beta_male)
  if (S_t0 <= 0) return(0)

  # We'll sum contributions of conditional survival over each remaining segment:
  # For interval j >= k0:
  #   segment start a_j = max(t0, cuts[j]), end b_j = cuts[j+1]
  #   Remaining time in interval j from a_j to b_j: L_j = b_j - a_j (possibly Inf for last)
  # Let S_cond(u) = S(u)/S(t0) for u >= t0.
  # Within interval j, hazard is constant h_j, so S_cond from a_j is exp(-h_j*(u - a_j))
  # Contribution to integral over [a_j, b_j) is:
  #   if finite L_j: ∫_0^{L_j} exp(-h_j s) * C_j ds = C_j * (1 - exp(-h_j L_j))/h_j
  #   if infinite:   C_j * (1/h_j)
  # where C_j is the carry-over multiplier = S(a_j)/S(t0) accumulated from previous intervals.
  # We compute sequentially.
  total <- 0
  C <- 1.0  # carry-over factor, S(a_current)/S(t0)

  # Handle the first (current) interval j = k0 with partial width from t0 to its right bound
  j <- k0
  a_j <- t0
  b_j <- cuts[j + 1]
  L_j <- b_j - a_j
  hj <- hvec[j]

  # Add contribution for current interval
  if (is.infinite(L_j)) {
    total <- total + C * (1 / hj)
    return(total)  # nothing beyond infinity
  } else {
    total <- total + C * (1 - exp(-hj * L_j)) / hj
    # Update carry-over to the next interval start:
    C <- C * exp(-hj * L_j)
  }

  # Subsequent full intervals
  if (j + 1 <= K) {
    for (jj in (j + 1):K) {
      hjj <- hvec[jj]
      a_jj <- cuts[jj]
      b_jj <- cuts[jj + 1]
      L_jj <- b_jj - a_jj

      if (is.infinite(L_jj)) {
        total <- total + C * (1 / hjj)
        break
      } else {
        total <- total + C * (1 - exp(-hjj * L_jj)) / hjj
        C <- C * exp(-hjj * L_jj)
      }
    }
  }
  total
}

# Wrapper to compute MRL for each subject at a common landmark t0
compute_mrl_for_df <- function(df, t0, cuts, h0_by_interval, beta_age, beta_male) {
  # Only subjects known to be alive at t0 (i.e., observed time >= t0) can have conditional MRL well-defined from observed data standpoint.
  # For modeling-based predictions, we can compute MRL for all covariate profiles; we report both:
  with(df, sapply(seq_len(nrow(df)), function(i) {
    mrl_piecewise(t0 = t0,
                  age = df$age[i],
                  gender = df$gender[i],
                  cuts = cuts,
                  h0_by_interval = h0_by_interval,
                  beta_age = beta_age,
                  beta_male = beta_male)
  }))
}

# -----------------------------

import backtrader as bt
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Iterable, Tuple, Union, Optional, Dict

DateLike = Union[datetime, float, int, str]


class EntryLine(bt.Indicator):
    """
    Draw an 'entryprice' line by passing the K-line timestamp and the price.

    Features
    - Match by timestamp with stable second-resolution keys to avoid float precision issues.
    - Can back-fill a matched bar immediately by reverse-iterating the loaded data buffer.
    - If the target bar hasn't been delivered yet, it will be drawn when that bar arrives.

    Public API
    - set_entryprice(when, price):
        * when: datetime/str(bt-parsable)/bt float date number
        * price: float

    Notes
    - If 'when' refers to a future bar (not yet in the loaded buffer), the price is stored
      and will be painted when 'next()' reaches that bar.
    - For timezones: if you pass a tz-aware datetime, it will be converted to UTC before matching.
    - If you pass a float or int, it is assumed to already be a backtrader date number
      (bt.date2num). Prefer passing datetime to avoid ambiguity with epoch seconds.
    """

    lines = ('entryprice',)
    plotinfo = dict(subplot=False)
    plotlines = dict(entryprice=dict(ls='-', lw=1, color='red'))

    def __init__(self):
        self.addminperiod(1)
        # key: int(round(bt_dtnum * 86400)) -> float(price)
        self._marks: Dict[int, float] = {}

    def prenext(self):
        self.lines.entryprice[0] = float('nan')

    def next(self):
        # Default to NaN
        self.lines.entryprice[0] = float('nan')

        # Current bar's datetime in bt's float day format
        dtnum = float(self.data.datetime[0])
        key = self._to_key(dtnum)

        price = self._marks.get(key)
        if price is not None:
            self.lines.entryprice[0] = float(price)

    def set_entryprice(self, when: DateLike, price: float) -> bool:
        """
        Set 'entryprice' for the bar that matches 'when' to 'price'.

        Returns True if the bar was found in the currently loaded data and updated immediately.
        Returns False if not found (it will be drawn automatically when that bar arrives).
        """
        key = self._to_key(when)
        price = float(price)

        # Try to locate in the already-delivered buffer using reverse iteration
        found, neg_index = self._locate_index_by_key(key)

        if found and neg_index is not None:
            # Update only the matched bar
            self.lines.entryprice[neg_index] = price
            return True

        # Not found in delivered bars: store for future matching in next()
        self._marks[key] = price
        return False

    def set_many(self, when_price_pairs: Iterable[Tuple[DateLike, float]]):
        for when, price in when_price_pairs:
            self.set_entryprice(when, price)

    # ---------------------------
    # Internal helpers
    # ---------------------------

    def _locate_index_by_key(self, key: int) -> Tuple[bool, Optional[int]]:
        """
        Reverse-iterate the loaded data buffer to find the negative index of a bar
        whose datetime matches the provided key (second-resolution).
        Returns (found, neg_index or None).
        """
        n = len(self.data)
        if n == 0:
            return False, None

        for j in range(-1, -n - 1, -1):  # -1, -2, ..., -n
            dtnum = float(self.data.datetime[j])
            if self._to_key(dtnum) == key:
                return True, j
        return False, None

    def _to_key(self, dt_or_num: DateLike) -> int:
        """
        Convert various datetime representations to a stable integer key
        based on backtrader's date number quantized to seconds.
        """
        dtnum = self._coerce_to_bt_dtnum(dt_or_num)
        return int(round(dtnum * 86400))

    @staticmethod
    def _coerce_to_bt_dtnum(dt_or_num: DateLike) -> float:
        """
        Convert input to backtrader's float day number.
        - tz-aware datetimes are converted to UTC before conversion
        """
        # Already a bt float day number
        if isinstance(dt_or_num, float):
            return dt_or_num

        if isinstance(dt_or_num, int):
            # Assume caller passed a bt date num already
            return float(dt_or_num)

        if isinstance(dt_or_num, str):
            # Try ISO-8601
            try:
                dt = datetime.fromisoformat(dt_or_num)
            except Exception as e:
                raise ValueError(f"Unable to parse datetime string: {dt_or_num}") from e
            if dt.tzinfo is not None:
                dt = dt.astimezone(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
            return bt.date2num(dt)

        if isinstance(dt_or_num, datetime):
            dt = dt_or_num
            if dt.tzinfo is not None:
                dt = dt.astimezone(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
            return bt.date2num(dt)

        # Fallback: try letting backtrader convert it (e.g., pandas.Timestamp)
        try:
            return bt.date2num(dt_or_num)
        except Exception as e:
            raise TypeError(f"Unsupported datetime type: {type(dt_or_num)}") from e

Provide assembler code for TASM (16-bit, .MODEL small) for MS-DOS that:
- Uses DOS interrupts only (no DPMI, no Windows APIs).
- Opens and reads from a text file named exactly "input.txt" in the current directory using INT 21h file I/O.
- Parses exactly 10 signed decimal integers (whitespace/newline separated; optional leading '+' or '-') from the file; ignore any extra content.
- Finds: (a) the minimum strictly positive element (>0) and its 1-based position among the 10; (b) the maximum strictly negative element (<0) and its 1-based position among the 10.
- If no positive (or no negative) element exists, output 0 for that position.
- Outputs to the console (INT 21h/AH=09h or 02h) two lines: "MinPosIndex: X" and "MaxNegIndex: Y" where X and Y are the 1-based positions or 0.

; TASM 16-bit small model program for MS-DOS
; - Opens "input.txt" in current directory
; - Reads and parses exactly 10 signed decimal integers (whitespace/newline separated)
; - Finds:
;     (a) minimum strictly positive element (>0) and its 1-based position
;     (b) maximum strictly negative element (<0) and its 1-based position
; - If category missing, outputs index 0
; - Outputs two lines:
;     "MinPosIndex: X"
;     "MaxNegIndex: Y"
; - Uses only DOS INT 21h (no DPMI/Windows APIs)
; - Clean exit via INT 21h/AH=4Ch
; Assemble: TASM prog.asm
; Link: TLINK prog.obj

.MODEL small
.STACK 256

.DATA
filename        db  'input.txt',0

; File buffer (enough for typical small inputs; we only need first 10 numbers)
BUF_SIZE        EQU 1024
fbuf            db  BUF_SIZE dup (0)
bytesRead       dw  0

; Parsed numbers (10 signed words)
nums            dw  10 dup (0)

; Output templates
msgMinLabel     db  'MinPosIndex: ',0
msgMaxLabel     db  'MaxNegIndex: ',0
crlf            db  13,10,'$'

; Output buffer for printing "label + index + CRLF"
; We'll print label with AH=09, then decimal index with a small routine, then CRLF with AH=09.
; Decimal print buffer (for number to string, max 5 digits for 1..32767, plus sign not used here)
decBuf          db  6 dup (0)   ; room for up to 5 digits + zero terminator (we'll use '$' method differently)

; Results
minPosVal       dw  0           ; best positive value (>0), 0 means not set
minPosIdx       dw  0           ; 1-based index or 0 if none

maxNegVal       dw  0           ; best negative value (<0), 0 means not set
maxNegIdx       dw  0           ; 1-based index or 0 if none

; Misc
fileHandle      dw  0

.CODE
start:
    mov ax, @data
    mov ds, ax

    ; Open file "input.txt" (INT 21h AH=3Dh, AL=0 read-only)
    mov ah, 3Dh
    mov al, 0
    mov dx, OFFSET filename
    int 21h
    jc  open_fail
    mov fileHandle, ax

    ; Read up to BUF_SIZE bytes
    mov ah, 3Fh
    mov bx, fileHandle
    mov cx, BUF_SIZE
    mov dx, OFFSET fbuf
    int 21h
    jc  read_fail
    mov bytesRead, ax

    ; Close file (we'll parse from memory)
    mov ah, 3Eh
    mov bx, fileHandle
    int 21h

    ; Parse exactly 10 integers from fbuf
    ; If fewer present, remaining will default to 0.
    lea si, fbuf
    mov cx, bytesRead
    lea di, nums
    mov bx, 10              ; numbers to parse
parse_loop_next_number:
    cmp bx, 0
    je  have_10
    ; Skip leading whitespace
skip_ws:
    cmp cx, 0
    je  end_of_input_pad_zero
    lodsb                   ; AL = [SI], SI++, CX--
    dec cx
    cmp al, ' '
    je  skip_ws
    cmp al, 9
    je  skip_ws
    cmp al, 13
    je  skip_ws
    cmp al, 10
    je  skip_ws
    ; Now AL is first non-space char: may be sign or digit
    mov dh, 0               ; sign: 0=positive, 1=negative
    cmp al, '+'
    je  got_sign_plus
    cmp al, '-'
    je  got_sign_minus
    jmp short got_first_char_checked
got_sign_plus:
    ; keep positive
    jmp short get_digits_start
got_sign_minus:
    mov dh, 1
    jmp short get_digits_start

got_first_char_checked:
    ; If not sign, we already have first char in AL to test as digit
    jmp short have_possible_digit

get_digits_start:
    ; Need next char after sign
    cmp cx, 0
    je  number_zero_store       ; sign without digits => treat as 0
    lodsb
    dec cx

have_possible_digit:
    ; Now AL should be a digit; if not, treat as 0 and continue
    mov ax, 0
    mov si_acc, ax              ; accumulator in AX, but TASM needs a label-free temp; we just use AX
    ; We already have AL = first char after optional sign
    cmp al, '0'
    jb  number_zero_store
    cmp al, '9'
    ja  number_zero_store

    ; Parse digits loop: AX = value (unsigned), up to overflow of 16-bit; we will clamp by natural wrap.
    ; We stop at first non-digit; SI currently points past AL due to LODSB usage.
    xor ax, ax                  ; AX = 0 accumulator
parse_digits:
    ; AL is current digit char
    sub al, '0'
    mov bl, al
    ; AX = AX*10 + BL
    mov dx, ax
    shl ax, 1                   ; ax*2
    mov di_acc, ax              ; temp store
    shl ax, 2                   ; ax*8 (from ax*2 -> *8)
    add ax, di_acc              ; ax = ax*10
    add ax, bx                  ; add digit (BL)
next_char_after_digit:
    ; Peek next char without losing it if not digit:
    cmp cx, 0
    je  digits_done
    lodsb
    dec cx
    cmp al, '0'
    jb  digits_done_storeback   ; AL holds non-digit for next phase (already consumed)
    cmp al, '9'
    ja  digits_done_storeback
    jmp short parse_digits

digits_done:
    ; No more chars; finished number
    jmp short finalize_number_no_pushback

digits_done_storeback:
    ; We've already consumed a non-digit in AL; keep it for next token:
    ; We'll "unget" it by moving SI back one and CX++
    dec si
    inc cx
    jmp short finalize_number_no_pushback

finalize_number_no_pushback:
    ; Apply sign in DH
    cmp dh, 0
    je  store_positive
    neg ax
store_positive:
    ; Store AX to nums[?]
    stosw
    dec bx
    jmp parse_loop_next_number

number_zero_store:
    ; Store 0 if malformed token or missing digits
    xor ax, ax
    stosw
    dec bx
    jmp parse_loop_next_number

end_of_input_pad_zero:
    ; If we run out of input, pad remaining numbers with 0
    xor ax, ax
pad_loop:
    cmp bx, 0
    je  have_10
    stosw
    dec bx
    jmp pad_loop

have_10:
    ; Compute min positive and max negative
    lea si, nums
    mov cx, 10
    xor dx, dx          ; index counter in DX (0..9)
    xor ax, ax
    mov minPosVal, ax
    mov minPosIdx, ax
    mov maxNegVal, ax
    mov maxNegIdx, ax

scan_loop:
    lodsw               ; AX = current number
    inc dx              ; 1-based index candidate
    ; Check positive (>0)
    cmp ax, 0
    jle check_negative
    ; If first positive (minPosIdx==0) or AX < minPosVal then update
    cmp word ptr minPosIdx, 0
    jne compare_minpos
    ; first positive
    mov minPosVal, ax
    mov minPosIdx, dx
    jmp short check_negative_done

compare_minpos:
    cmp ax, minPosVal
    jge check_negative_done
    mov minPosVal, ax
    mov minPosIdx, dx

check_negative:
    cmp ax, 0
    jge check_negative_done
    ; negative: want maximum (closest to zero)
    cmp word ptr maxNegIdx, 0
    jne compare_maxneg
    ; first negative
    mov maxNegVal, ax
    mov maxNegIdx, dx
    jmp short check_negative_done

compare_maxneg:
    ; if AX > maxNegVal then update (less negative)
    cmp ax, maxNegVal
    jle check_negative_done
    mov maxNegVal, ax
    mov maxNegIdx, dx

check_negative_done:
    loop scan_loop

    ; Output results
    ; Print "MinPosIndex: " then the index value as decimal, then CRLF
    mov dx, OFFSET msgMinLabel
    mov ah, 09h
    int 21h

    mov ax, minPosIdx
    call PrintDecUnsigned

    mov dx, OFFSET crlf
    mov ah, 09h
    int 21h

    ; Print "MaxNegIndex: " then the index value as decimal, then CRLF
    mov dx, OFFSET msgMaxLabel
    mov ah, 09h
    int 21h

    mov ax, maxNegIdx
    call PrintDecUnsigned

    mov dx, OFFSET crlf
    mov ah, 09h
    int 21h

    ; Exit to DOS
    mov ax, 4C00h
    int 21h

; ------------- Error handling: on failure, set indexes to 0 and print anyway -------------
open_fail:
read_fail:
    ; If file was opened, try close (BX has undefined; we only close if handle saved, but safe to skip)
    xor ax, ax
    mov minPosIdx, ax
    mov maxNegIdx, ax

    mov dx, OFFSET msgMinLabel
    mov ah, 09h
    int 21h
    mov ax, 0
    call PrintDecUnsigned
    mov dx, OFFSET crlf
    mov ah, 09h
    int 21h

    mov dx, OFFSET msgMaxLabel
    mov ah, 09h
    int 21h
    mov ax, 0
    call PrintDecUnsigned
    mov dx, OFFSET crlf
    mov ah, 09h
    int 21h

    mov ax, 4C00h
    int 21h

; ------------- Subroutines -------------

; PrintDecUnsigned
; Input: AX = unsigned 16-bit value (0..65535)
; Uses: BX, CX, DX, SI
; Output: prints the decimal representation using INT 21h/AH=02h for each char
PrintDecUnsigned PROC NEAR
    push ax
    push bx
    push cx
    push dx
    push si

    mov bx, 10
    mov cx, 0              ; digit count
    lea si, decBuf

    ; Special case zero
    cmp ax, 0
    jne pdu_divloop
    mov dl, '0'
    mov ah, 02h
    int 21h
    jmp pdu_done

pdu_divloop:
    ; Convert by repeated division, store remainders in decBuf
pdu_loop:
    xor dx, dx
    div bx                 ; AX = AX/10, DX = remainder
    add dl, '0'            ; DL = digit char
    mov [si], dl
    inc si
    inc cx
    cmp ax, 0
    jne pdu_loop

    ; Output digits in reverse
    dec si
pdu_out:
    mov dl, [si]
    mov ah, 02h
    int 21h
    dec si
    loop pdu_out

pdu_done:
    pop si
    pop dx
    pop cx
    pop bx
    pop ax
    ret
PrintDecUnsigned ENDP

; ------------- Temporary registers placeholders for clarity (no storage needed) -------------
; Note: The labels si_acc and di_acc are symbolic comments; TASM will ignore them if left as comments.
; We kept operations directly in AX/BX with minimal temps.

END start

Provide TASM (MASM/TASM syntax, 16-bit) assembler code for DOS (COM or MZ EXE) that:
- Uses DOS INT 21h file APIs to open 'input.txt' in the current directory and read exactly 10 signed 16-bit integers in text form (decimal, separated by spaces/newlines). Stop after 10 numbers even if the file is longer; if the file has fewer than 10 numbers, treat missing values as not present and still proceed.
- Parses ASCII to signed 16-bit values (handles optional leading '+' or '-' and ignores leading whitespace between numbers).
- Finds the minimum strictly positive value (>0) and its 0-based index position among the 10, and the maximum strictly negative value (<0) and its 0-based index.
- Outputs to the DOS console using INT 21h/AH=09h two lines in this exact format:
  MinPosIndex: <index or 0 if none>
  MaxNegIndex: <index or 0 if none>
- If no positive (or no negative) element exists among the read values, output 0 for that index.
- Assembles with TASM and links for DOS; include .model/.code segments, proper data segment setup (mov ax,@data / mov ds,ax), and comments explaining the logic.

; TASM/MASM 16-bit DOS program (MZ .EXE) that:
; - Opens "input.txt" in current directory
; - Reads ASCII decimal signed integers separated by spaces/newlines
; - Takes up to 10 numbers (stop after 10 even if more)
; - Finds min strictly positive (>0) and its 0-based index
; - Finds max strictly negative (<0) and its 0-based index
; - Prints:
;     MinPosIndex: <index or 0 if none>
;     MaxNegIndex: <index or 0 if none>
; - If no positive/negative found, prints 0 for that index
;
; Assemble:  tasm prog.asm
; Link:      tlink prog
; Run under DOS (or DOSBox)

.model small
.stack 256

.data
filename        db 'input.txt',0

; Read buffer for file (4KB is plenty for typical input)
BUF_SIZE        equ 4096
readBuf         db BUF_SIZE dup(?)
bytesInBuf      dw 0            ; valid bytes in buffer
bufPos          dw 0            ; current parse position in buffer
fileHandle      dw 0

; Parsed numbers storage (up to 10)
NUM_COUNT       equ 10
nums            dw NUM_COUNT dup(0)
haveCount       dw 0            ; how many numbers actually parsed (<=10)

; Tracking min positive and max negative
minPosVal       dw 7FFFh        ; sentinel large positive
minPosIdx       dw 0FFFFh       ; 0xFFFF means "not found"
maxNegVal       dw 8000h        ; sentinel most negative (will be increased)
maxNegIdx       dw 0FFFFh       ; 0xFFFF means "not found"

; Output strings (terminated with '$' for AH=09h)
outMinLabel     db 'MinPosIndex: $'
outCRLF         db 13,10,'$'
outMaxLabel     db 'MaxNegIndex: $'

; Buffer to print decimal of index (0..9) as text
; We only ever need single digit 0..9 for output index or 0.
idxStr          db '0','$'

.code

;----------------------------------------------------------
; PrintZeroTermDollar: prints DS:DX string ending at '$'
; IN: DS:DX -> string
;----------------------------------------------------------
PrintStr proc
    mov ah,09h
    int 21h
    ret
PrintStr endp

;----------------------------------------------------------
; PrintCRLF: prints CRLF
;----------------------------------------------------------
PrintCRLF proc
    lea dx, outCRLF
    call PrintStr
    ret
PrintCRLF endp

;----------------------------------------------------------
; PrintIndexInDx: prints decimal digit 0..9 in DL
; Uses idxStr buffer
; IN: DL = 0..9
;----------------------------------------------------------
PrintIndexInDl proc
    push ax
    push dx
    lea dx, idxStr
    mov al, dl
    add al, '0'
    mov [idxStr], al
    call PrintStr
    pop dx
    pop ax
    ret
PrintIndexInDl endp

;----------------------------------------------------------
; OpenFile: opens input.txt for read-only
; OUT: CF clear = success, AX=handle; CF set = error
;----------------------------------------------------------
OpenFile proc
    lea dx, filename
    mov ax,3D00h         ; open existing, read-only
    int 21h
    ret
OpenFile endp

;----------------------------------------------------------
; ReadChunk: fills readBuf, sets bytesInBuf and bufPos
; OUT: CF clear = success (AX=bytes read), CF set = error
;----------------------------------------------------------
ReadChunk proc
    mov bx, fileHandle
    lea dx, readBuf
    mov cx, BUF_SIZE
    mov ah,3Fh
    int 21h
    jc  rc_err
    ; AX = bytes read (may be 0 at EOF)
    mov bytesInBuf, ax
    mov bufPos, 0
    clc
    ret
rc_err:
    stc
    ret
ReadChunk endp

;----------------------------------------------------------
; GetChar: fetch next char from buffer, refilling if needed
; OUT: AL=char, CF clear if got a char
;      CF set if EOF (no more chars)
; Destroys: AX
;----------------------------------------------------------
GetChar proc
.next:
    mov ax, bufPos
    cmp ax, bytesInBuf
    jb  have
    ; need to read more
    call ReadChunk
    jc  eof_set
    cmp bytesInBuf, 0
    je  eof_set
    jmp .next
have:
    ; AL = readBuf[bufPos]
    lea dx, readBuf
    add dx, ax
    mov al, [dx]
    inc ax
    mov bufPos, ax
    clc
    ret
eof_set:
    stc
    ret
GetChar endp

;----------------------------------------------------------
; UngetChar: steps back one character in buffer (if possible)
; Used when we've read one char beyond a token.
;----------------------------------------------------------
UngetChar proc
    mov ax, bufPos
    or  ax, ax
    jz  ug_exit          ; can't unget past start of buffer; safe to ignore
    dec ax
    mov bufPos, ax
ug_exit:
    ret
UngetChar endp

;----------------------------------------------------------
; SkipWhitespace: advances past spaces, tabs, CR, LF
; OUT: AL = first non-ws char (left in buffer via Unget), or EOF (CF set)
; Keeps the non-ws char available (by ungetting it).
;----------------------------------------------------------
SkipWhitespace proc
    push ax
    push bx
sw_next:
    call GetChar
    jc  sw_eof
    mov bl, al
    cmp bl, ' '
    je  sw_next
    cmp bl, 9
    je  sw_next
    cmp bl, 13
    je  sw_next
    cmp bl, 10
    je  sw_next
    ; non-ws found, unget it and return
    call UngetChar
    clc
    pop bx
    pop ax
    ret
sw_eof:
    stc
    pop bx
    pop ax
    ret
SkipWhitespace endp

;----------------------------------------------------------
; ParseInt16: parses optional sign and digits into AX (signed 16-bit)
; Returns CF clear on success with AX=value.
; If no digits found before EOF or non-digit, returns CF set.
; Advances buffer past the parsed number, leaves next char unread.
; Handles optional leading '+' or '-'.
; NOTE: Does not detect overflow; values that exceed 16-bit will wrap.
;----------------------------------------------------------
ParseInt16 proc
    push bx
    push cx
    push dx
    ; skip whitespace first
    call SkipWhitespace
    jc  pi_fail

    ; read optional sign
    mov bl, 0           ; sign = 0 means positive, 1 means negative
    call GetChar
    jc  pi_fail
    cmp al, '+'
    je  got_sign
    cmp al, '-'
    je  got_neg
    ; no sign, push back
    call UngetChar
    jmp  read_digits
got_sign:
    ; sign was '+', continue
    jmp  read_digits
got_neg:
    mov bl, 1
read_digits:
    xor ax, ax          ; AX = accumulator
    mov cx, 0           ; digit count
pd_loop:
    call GetChar
    jc  pd_end_no_digits
    cmp al, '0'
    jb  pd_non_digit
    cmp al, '9'
    ja  pd_non_digit
    ; digit
    sub al, '0'
    ; AX = AX*10 + AL
    mov dl, al
    mov bx, ax
    shl ax,1            ; AX = AX*2
    mov dx, ax
    shl ax,1            ; AX = AX*4
    add ax, dx          ; AX = AX*6
    add ax, bx          ; AX = AX*7
    shl ax,1            ; AX = AX*14
    add ax, dl          ; AX = AX*14 + digit -> actually 10*orig + digit
    inc cx
    jmp pd_loop
pd_non_digit:
    ; not a digit, push it back
    call UngetChar
    jmp pd_end
pd_end_no_digits:
    ; EOF while trying, if no digits read it's a failure
pd_end:
    cmp cx, 0
    je  pi_fail         ; no digits at all -> fail

    ; apply sign if needed
    ; if negative, AX = -AX
    push ax
    cmp bl, 0
    je  pi_ok
    neg ax
pi_ok:
    clc
    pop dx              ; clean temp pushed AX
    pop dx
    pop cx
    pop bx
    ret
pi_fail:
    stc
    pop dx
    pop cx
    pop bx
    ret
ParseInt16 endp

;----------------------------------------------------------
; Main
;----------------------------------------------------------
start:
    mov ax,@data
    mov ds,ax

    ; Open file
    call OpenFile
    jc  after_io             ; if fail, proceed as if 0 numbers
    mov fileHandle, ax

    ; Prime buffer
    call ReadChunk
    jc  close_and_go
    ; bytesInBuf may be 0 at EOF; still okay

    ; Parse up to NUM_COUNT numbers
    xor cx, cx               ; CX = count
parse_loop:
    cmp cx, NUM_COUNT
    jae done_parse
    push cx
    call ParseInt16
    jc  no_more_nums         ; stop on failure/EOF (treat missing as not present)
    ; store AX into nums[cx]
    pop bx                   ; restore index in BX
    mov si, bx
    shl si,1
    mov [nums+si], ax
    inc bx
    mov cx, bx
    jmp parse_loop
no_more_nums:
    pop cx                   ; restore CX
done_parse:
    mov haveCount, cx

close_and_go:
    ; Close file if opened
    mov bx, fileHandle
    or  bx, bx
    jz  after_io
    mov ah,3Eh
    int 21h

after_io:
    ; Process exactly haveCount numbers (<=10)
    xor bx, bx               ; BX = i
proc_loop:
    cmp bx, haveCount
    jae proc_done
    mov si, bx
    shl si,1
    mov ax, [nums+si]

    ; Check positive (>0): update min positive
    cmp ax, 0
    jle chk_negative
    ; if ax < minPosVal -> update
    mov dx, minPosVal
    cmp ax, dx
    jge chk_negative
    mov minPosVal, ax
    mov minPosIdx, bx
chk_negative:
    ; Check negative (<0): update max negative (closest to zero)
    cmp ax, 0
    jge next_i
    ; if ax > maxNegVal -> update (less negative)
    mov dx, maxNegVal
    cmp ax, dx
    jle next_i
    mov maxNegVal, ax
    mov maxNegIdx, bx
next_i:
    inc bx
    jmp proc_loop

proc_done:
    ; Prepare output: print labels and indexes
    ; MinPosIndex:
    lea dx, outMinLabel
    call PrintStr
    ; Decide value to print
    mov dx, minPosIdx
    cmp dx, 0FFFFh
    jne have_minpos
    mov dl, 0              ; not found -> print 0
    jmp print_min
have_minpos:
    ; Ensure within 0..9; haveCount<=10, index<10 if present
    mov dl, byte ptr minPosIdx
print_min:
    call PrintIndexInDl
    call PrintCRLF

    ; MaxNegIndex:
    lea dx, outMaxLabel
    call PrintStr
    mov dx, maxNegIdx
    cmp dx, 0FFFFh
    jne have_maxneg
    mov dl, 0
    jmp print_max
have_maxneg:
    mov dl, byte ptr maxNegIdx
print_max:
